vulnerabilities.name: SQL Injection — Login Bypass
vulnerabilities.description: The login form interpolates user input directly into a SQL query using Python string formatting. An attacker can bypass authentication entirely.
vulnerabilities.hint: Try entering ' OR 1=1 -- as the username with any password.
vulnerabilities.fix: Use parameterized queries with ? placeholders instead of string interpolation.

vulnerabilities.name: SQL Injection — Search (UNION-based)
vulnerabilities.description: The search query parameter is interpolated into a SQL LIKE clause. UNION-based injection can extract data from other tables.
vulnerabilities.hint: Try: ' UNION SELECT id,username,password,bio,role,created_at FROM users --

vulnerabilities.name: OS Command Injection (RCE)
vulnerabilities.description: User input is passed directly to a shell command via subprocess with shell=True. An attacker can chain arbitrary commands.
vulnerabilities.fix: Use subprocess with shell=False and pass arguments as a list. Validate input against a whitelist of allowed characters.

vulnerabilities.name: Stored XSS — Comments
vulnerabilities.description: Comment body is rendered with Jinja2's |safe filter, bypassing auto-escaping. Any HTML or JavaScript in a comment executes in every visitor's browser.
vulnerabilities.fix: Remove the |safe filter from the comment body rendering.

vulnerabilities.name: Stored XSS — Profile Bio
vulnerabilities.description: The user bio field is rendered with |safe in the profile template. Any HTML or JavaScript stored in the bio executes when viewing the profile.
vulnerabilities.hint: Edit your bio to:
vulnerabilities.fix: Remove the |safe filter from the bio rendering.

vulnerabilities.name: Broken Access Control — Admin Dashboard
vulnerabilities.description: The admin dashboard and all admin routes have no authentication or authorization checks. Any visitor can access /admin and manage posts and users.
vulnerabilities.hint: Simply navigate to /admin/ without logging in.
vulnerabilities.fix: Add a @login_required decorator and verify the user's role is 'admin' before processing admin requests.

vulnerabilities.name: IDOR — Draft Post Access
vulnerabilities.description: The post detail route does not check whether a post is published or whether the requesting user is the author. Draft posts are accessible by guessing or enumerating IDs.
vulnerabilities.hint: Navigate to /post/5 to see a confidential draft post.
vulnerabilities.fix: Check post.status == 'published' or verify the requesting user is the post's author.

vulnerabilities.name: IDOR — Profile Edit
vulnerabilities.description: Any logged-in user can edit any other user's profile. There is no check that the session user matches the profile being edited.
vulnerabilities.hint: Log in as any user and navigate to /user/admin/edit to modify the admin's bio.
vulnerabilities.fix: Verify session['username'] matches the username in the URL before allowing edits.

vulnerabilities.name: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF)
vulnerabilities.description: The weather widget fetches any URL provided by the user, including internal services, cloud metadata endpoints, and local files.
vulnerabilities.fix: Validate the URL against an allowlist of permitted domains. Block private IP ranges and metadata endpoints.

vulnerabilities.name: Unrestricted File Upload
vulnerabilities.description: Files are uploaded without any validation of extension, MIME type, or content. Uploaded .html files are served inline, enabling stored XSS. Other dangerous file types (.py, .sh) can also be uploaded.
vulnerabilities.hint: Upload an HTML file containing <script>alert('XSS')</script> and then visit the uploaded file URL.
vulnerabilities.fix: Validate file extension against an allowlist. Set Content-Disposition: attachment when serving uploads. Validate MIME type.

vulnerabilities.name: Information Exposure — Debug Endpoint
vulnerabilities.description: The /debug endpoint exposes environment variables, application configuration (including SECRET_KEY), database schema, Python version, and system information to any visitor.
vulnerabilities.fix: Remove the debug endpoint entirely, or gate it behind admin authentication.

vulnerabilities.name: Hardcoded Secret Key
vulnerabilities.description: The Flask SECRET_KEY is hardcoded as 'dev'. This allows an attacker to forge session cookies and impersonate any user, including admins.
vulnerabilities.hint: The secret key is visible in config.py and on the /debug endpoint. Use flask-unsign to forge cookies.
vulnerabilities.fix: Generate a random secret key and load it from an environment variable.

vulnerabilities.name: Weak Password Hashing (MD5)
vulnerabilities.description: Passwords are hashed with unsalted MD5, which is trivially crackable. MD5 is not a password hashing algorithm.
vulnerabilities.hint: Extract password hashes via SQLi on /search, then crack them with any MD5 lookup table.
vulnerabilities.fix: Use bcrypt or argon2 for password hashing.

vulnerabilities.name: Insecure Session Cookie Flags
vulnerabilities.description: Session cookies are set without HttpOnly and Secure flags. This allows JavaScript to read session cookies (enabling XSS-based session hijacking) and cookies to be sent over unencrypted HTTP.
vulnerabilities.hint: Use browser DevTools to read document.cookie after exploiting an XSS vulnerability.
vulnerabilities.fix: Set SESSION_COOKIE_HTTPONLY = True and SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE = True.

vulnerabilities.name: Debug Mode Enabled
vulnerabilities.description: Flask debug mode is enabled, exposing the interactive Werkzeug debugger on unhandled exceptions. An attacker can execute arbitrary Python code through the debugger console.
vulnerabilities.hint: Trigger an error (e.g., visit a route that throws an exception) and use the interactive debugger PIN shown in the console.
